bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to unemployment benefits; requiring a fraud reporting portal for employers; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 268.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[268.1821] FRAUD REPORTING PORTAL.

Subdivision 1.

Creation of fraud reporting portal.

The commissioner shall provide a portal for employers to report information regarding potential applicant fraud. The commissioner may add the reporting elements listed in subdivision 2 to an existing online fraud reporting system accessible by employers.

Subd. 2.

Reporting elements.

At a minimum, the following elements must be included as part of the fraud reporting portal:

(1) that an applicant was a no-show for a scheduled interview;

(2) that an applicant refused an offer of work by the employer; and

(3) that the employer was unable to contact the applicant for an interview, an offer of work, or a recall to work.

Subd. 3.

Outreach.

The commissioner must conduct outreach to communicate to employers the availability of the fraud reporting portal.

Subd. 4.

Access to applicant data.

Notwithstanding section 268.19 or any other law to the contrary, upon request by a prospective employer, the commissioner must provide the following data, including data classified as private data on individuals:

(1) an applicant's no-show record; and

(2) an applicant's refusal to work record.
additions: The commissioner shall provide a portal for employers to report information regarding potential applicant fraud. The commissioner may add the reporting elements listed in subdivision 2 to an existing online fraud reporting system accessible by employers.
At a minimum, the following elements must be included as part of the fraud reporting portal:
(1) that an applicant was a no-show for a scheduled interview;
(2) that an applicant refused an offer of work by the employer; and
(3) that the employer was unable to contact the applicant for an interview, an offer of work, or a recall to work.
The commissioner must conduct outreach to communicate to employers the availability of the fraud reporting portal.

Notwithstanding section 268.19 or any other law to the contrary, upon request by a prospective employer, the commissioner must provide the following data, including data classified as private data on individuals:
(2) an applicant's refusal to work record.
